subject: Ombrex - retry amplification & elevated 5xx/429: customer updates + mitigation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@ombrex.com>, support@ombrex.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Ombrex - transient retry amplification impacting API (5xx/429)

Hi Daniel / Ombrex team,

We detected a spike in 5xx and 429 responses originating from the v2 inference route serving your production keys starting ~08:55 PST. Metrics show a correlated surge in client retries from several of your hosts which looks like a retry-amplification loop: higher latency -> more retries -> increased load -> more 5xx/429.

What we're seeing: 
- Global 5xx rate on your keys increased from ~0.2% baseline to ~6% during the window.
- Median p50 latency jumped from 120ms to 1.2s; p95s are near 7s.
- The majority of 429s were from our ingress throttling reacting to sustained queue pressure.

Immediate ask: can you confirm if you rolled any client-side retry changes or traffic increases at ~08:50? If you can temporarily throttle your request fanout/backoff that will reduce amplification while we mitigate on our side.

Planned short-term mitigations (we're initiating these now):
1) Deploy adaptive ingress throttling configuration targeted at your API key to enforce graded Retry-After hints (preferred to immediate hard limits).
2) Push a guard in the request router to return a 503 + Retry-After 60 for sustained overload to break retry loops.
3) Enable per-API-key circuit breaking to cap concurrency and protect other customers.

I'll coordinate a call if you'd like — otherwise we'll proceed with the mitigations above and send updates every 30-60 minutes. ETA for initial changes: ~2 hours.

Attachments: I'll attach an anonymized error sample and the small throttle patch we're proposing.

Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Daniel Park <daniel@ombrex.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, support@ombrex.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:18:23 -0800
Subject: Re: Ombrex - transient retry amplification impacting API (5xx/429)

Jonas — thanks for the quick heads up.

We did deploy a small client patch last night that increased the default concurrency window for our inference clients (to improve throughput), but nothing that should spike traffic now. We are seeing the same 5xx/429s across three regions and are rolling back the change as a precaution.

Two quick questions: 
1) Is there any data loss risk for requests that returned 5xx?
2) Can you share an ETA for when normal latency will be restored?

I attached a short log snippet from our side (error IDs and timestamps). We'll throttle our clients immediately and will be on standby for a call.

—Daniel
Senior SRE, Ombrex
daniel@ombrex.com

Subject: RE: Ombrex - transient retry amplification impacting API (5xx/429)

Jonas / team — internal runbook steps I'm initiating: 

Action plan (short term, prioritized):
- OWNER: Sean — enable per-key dynamic ingress throttling and set Retry-After hints (rollout to production across edge nodes).
- OWNER: Infra team (assigned by Sean) — deploy small router guard that converts sustained queueing into 503 + Retry-After 60 to break amplification (canary to 10% traffic). Patch: dynamic-throttle.patch.diff (attached).
- OWNER: Laura — lead customer comms, confirm rollback status with Ombrex and prep exec note if they request credits.
- OWNER: Jonas — coordinate escalation with Sales/Account and confirm SLA implications.

Monitoring: Create Grafana panel for key-level 5xx and client-side retry rate; set an alert threshold at 1.5% 5xx across 5 minutes to trigger immediate manual rollback of throttling config if we see customer impact beyond acceptable.

We should aim to have the first mitigation in canary within ~90 minutes and a wider rollout in 2-3 hours if metrics look good.

Marissa
Senior Manager, Customer Ops
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@ombrex.com>, support@ombrex.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Ombrex - transient retry amplification impacting API (5xx/429)

Daniel — thanks for confirming the client-side change and for throttling on your end. A few clarifications: 
- 5xx responses are transient failures at the service edge; we do not drop persistent request receipts — there is no backend data loss for requests that returned 5xx, but those requests will need to be retried if the client requires successful completion.
- Our immediate target is to reduce amplification and restore p50/p95 latency to baseline. We're pushing the routing guard into canary first, then will expand.

Planned timeline (tentative):
- 10:15 PST: canary deploy of router guard + Retry-After hints to 10% of Ombrex traffic
- 11:30 PST: validate metrics; if 5xxs drop >40% and p95 improves, expand to 50%
- 12:45 PST: wider rollout remainder if stable; otherwise rollback and escalate to emergency infra window.

I'll update you after canary checks. Status page incident: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2027-02-15-ombrex

Jonas

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:50:05 -0700
Subject: RE: Ombrex - retry amplification update (canary metrics)

Quick update — canary results:
- Canary (10% Ombrex traffic) deployed at 10:16 PST. 5xx rate on canary dropped from 6.1% -> 2.2% within 20 mins.
- p95 latency on canary improved from ~7s -> ~1.8s.
- Overall client retry rate for canary group down ~58%.

Next steps: expanding to 50% at 11:35 PST. Monitoring closely; will pause if we see customer requests failing with the new Retry-After behavior beyond acceptable thresholds.

Also setting up a short postmortem doc and proposed follow-up call for tomorrow to review root cause and longer-term hardening.

Attachments: dynamic-throttle.patch.diff (details of router guard), anonymized error sample included.

Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@ombrex.com>, support@ombrex.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Ombrex - mitigation complete, recommended client backoff and follow-up

Daniel — final update for this thread:
- We completed the full rollout of the router guard and per-key throttles at 12:05 PST. Post-rollout metrics show 5xxs reduced to 0.4% and 429s back to baseline within 25 minutes. Latency p95 is back under 900ms for your keys.
- We did not detect any persistent data loss; requests that received 5xx/429 will need retry by the client as appropriate.
- Actions for Ombrex: implement jittered exponential backoff client-side and reduce aggressive concurrency for short windows after failures; we can share a suggested client config if helpful.

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule a 60-minute postmortem tomorrow to review root cause, telemetry gaps, and permanent throttling strategy.
2) Share the postmortem and proposed SDK changes (we'll draft).
3) If you want a formal credit review, loop in your account exec (Laura) and we'll present the options.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — we will keep the incident open on the status page for 48 hours while we watch for regressions.

Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
